steps.title: Start the potatoes
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Set out {{ingredients}}. Quarter the baby potatoes into similar pieces, toss with enough olive oil to coat and salt to taste, and spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet pan. Roast about 20–25 minutes, checking for browned edges and a center that yields easily to a knife; continue as needed. Check that all the measured thighs fit without overlap in your oven-safe skillet; use a baking dish for the chicken finish if needed. Prepare the chicken and sauce while the potatoes roast. The optional cooking spray is for the baking-dish variation below, which uses a different oven temperature and omits the separate potato roast.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Use {{ingredients}}: pat chicken dry with paper towels, then season with Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden, about 5–7 minutes, then brown the other side for about 2 minutes. Work in batches if needed, reducing heat if the butter or fond begins to burn. Transfer to a plate reserved for partly cooked chicken; continue directly with the recipe.

steps.title: Wilt the spinach
steps.text: Use {{ingredients}}: melt the butter for this step in the skillet, add spinach and stir until it begins to wilt, about 2 minutes. Transfer spinach to a bowl. Pour off excessive rendered chicken fat, keeping the browned fond and leaving no burned bits.

steps.title: Make the roux
steps.text: Use {{ingredients}}: melt the sauce butter over medium heat. Add garlic and stir until fragrant, about 1–2 minutes, without browning it. Whisk in flour and cook about 1 minute, stirring until smooth and lightly colored.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Use {{ingredients}}: gradually whisk broth into the roux with thyme and basil, loosening the browned fond. Simmer gently, whisking, until smooth and lightly thickened, about 1–2 minutes. Lower the heat and stir in cream and Parmesan, about 1–2 minutes, until the cheese melts. Do not boil hard after adding cheese. The sauce has contacted partly cooked chicken fond; wait until the final bake is complete before tasting it.

steps.title: Finish the chicken in sauce
steps.text: Stir the wilted spinach into the sauce and return the seared chicken skin-side up. Keep as much skin above the sauce as possible. If your oven-safe skillet cannot hold the thighs in one layer, transfer chicken, spinach and sauce to a baking dish large enough to fit them without overlap. Keep the roasted potatoes separate for crispness; adding them to the sauce will soften their surface.

steps.title: Bake and measure
steps.text: Transfer the skillet or chicken baking dish to the 425°F oven. Begin checking after about 10 minutes; the thickest part of every thigh, away from bone, and the sauce at the center must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue baking as needed; ten minutes is a first check, not a guarantee of completion. If the skin darkens early, shield it loosely with foil while the meat finishes. Check the separately roasted potatoes for tenderness as well. Rest safely cooked chicken 5 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: After the bake meets the temperature checks, taste the sauce with a clean spoon. Use {{ingredients}}: adjust salt and pepper, then add parsley if using. Serve one thigh per portion with potatoes, spinach and sauce.

after.focus: Coordinate seared chicken and potatoes in a cream-sauce bake
after.outcome: Browned chicken above a smooth sauce, separately roasted fork-tender potatoes, and every thigh at 165°F / 74°C.
before: Check that the measured thighs fit in one layer in your oven-safe skillet, and that potatoes fit in one layer on a sheet pan. Scaling can require more pans or a baking dish for the chicken finish.
Quarter baby potatoes evenly. Start their roast first and prepare the sauce while they cook. Have separate plates for partly cooked and finished chicken; continue directly to the oven finish.

checkpoints.cue: Chicken skin is golden, while the pan fond is brown rather than black.
checkpoints.why: Browning builds flavor; burned butter and fond make the sauce bitter.

checkpoints.cue: The sauce is smooth and lightly coats a spoon before assembly.
checkpoints.why: Whisking liquid gradually into the flour mixture avoids lumps; high heat after cheese can make the sauce grainy.

checkpoints.cue: Each thigh and the sauce center are at least 165°F / 74°C, and a knife passes easily through the separately roasted potatoes.
checkpoints.why: Meat size and potato size vary, so one endpoint cannot stand in for the other.

troubleshooting.problem: Chicken is ready but potatoes are firm
troubleshooting.cause: Large or uneven potato quarters cook more slowly.
troubleshooting.fix: Continue the separate potato roast until tender, keeping safely cooked chicken warm for serving. For the sauced-potato variation, move cooked chicken to a clean plate while potatoes finish in the dish. Cut more uniform pieces next time.

troubleshooting.cause: The cheese boiled hard, or too much rendered chicken fat remained.
troubleshooting.fix: Lower the heat and stir gently. A badly separated cheese sauce may not become smooth again; keep the sauce below a hard boil in the next batch.

troubleshooting.cause: Sauce and steam wetted the seared skin.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep skin above the sauce during baking and serve promptly. Skin submerged in sauce will not retain a shattering crust.

substitutions.effect: A lighter, less rich sauce that still uses the same flour thickener; avoid a hard boil after adding dairy.

substitutions.alternative: Larger potatoes cut into similar small pieces
substitutions.effect: The potato variety affects texture and larger pieces take longer; check with a knife rather than using time alone.

after.timing: 20 minutes prep plus roughly 45–60 minutes cooking and a 5-minute rest gives a 70–85 minute planning range. Start roasting potatoes while searing chicken and making sauce. Begin checking the skillet finish at ten minutes and continue to the measured endpoints. The sauced-potato variation starts checking at 25–30 minutes. Active work is roughly 30–35 minutes; extra pans, large thighs or large potato pieces may extend elapsed time.
after.storage: Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C), at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use cooked chicken within 3–4 days and reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Store roasted potatoes separately from sauce. Reheat chicken and sauce covered, and potatoes uncovered, to the endpoint; the sauce and spinach soften chicken skin, and reheating may separate the sauce.

## Chef's Note

This is a French-meets-Italian one-skillet dinner - skin-on thighs seared until the fat renders and the skin shatters, then finished in a garlic-Parmesan cream sauce with roasted potatoes. The sear is non-negotiable: 5-7 minutes skin-side down without touching builds the crust. The fond left in the pan becomes the base of your sauce - deglaze with broth, whisk in cream and Parmesan, and you have a weeknight version of chicken fricassee.

## Directions

1.  **Roast Potatoes:** Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss potatoes with oil and salt. Roast on a sheet pan for 20-25 minutes until crispy.
2.  **Sear Chicken:** Season chicken with Italian seasoning. In a large oven-safe skillet, sear chicken skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove to a plate.
3.  **The Sauce:** Wipe out excess fat. Melt butter in the skillet. Add garlic for 30 seconds. Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute (The Roux).
4.  **Emulsify:** Gradually whisk in broth and cream until thickened. Stir in the Parmesan and spinach until wilted.
5.  **Combine:** Return the chicken and the **crispy roasted potatoes** to the skillet.
6.  **Finish:** Transfer the skillet to the oven for 10 minutes to finish cooking the chicken (165°F). Serve immediately.

## Chef's Note

These chicken thighs finish in a garlic-Parmesan cream sauce with spinach, while the potatoes roast separately. Keep the potatoes beside the sauce at serving if you want their browned edges to remain crisp; sauce contact softens them. Brown the chicken first, then use temperature rather than skin color to judge the oven finish.

## Directions

1. **Start the potatoes:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. Set out cooking spray (if using), olive oil, baby potatoes, and salt. Quarter the baby potatoes into similar pieces, toss with enough olive oil to coat and salt to taste, and spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet pan. Roast about 20–25 minutes, checking for browned edges and a center that yields easily to a knife; continue as needed. Check that all the measured thighs fit without overlap in your oven-safe skillet; use a baking dish for the chicken finish if needed. Prepare the chicken and sauce while the potatoes roast. The optional cooking spray is for the baking-dish variation below, which uses a different oven temperature and omits the separate potato roast.
2. **Brown the chicken:** Use bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, Italian seasoning, salt, black pepper, and unsalted butter: pat chicken dry with paper towels, then season with Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden, about 5–7 minutes, then brown the other side for about 2 minutes. Work in batches if needed, reducing heat if the butter or fond begins to burn. Transfer to a plate reserved for partly cooked chicken; continue directly with the recipe.
3. **Wilt the spinach:** Use unsalted butter and baby spinach: melt the butter for this step in the skillet, add spinach and stir until it begins to wilt, about 2 minutes. Transfer spinach to a bowl. Pour off excessive rendered chicken fat, keeping the browned fond and leaving no burned bits.
4. **Make the roux:** Use unsalted butter, garlic cloves, and all-purpose flour: melt the sauce butter over medium heat. Add garlic and stir until fragrant, about 1–2 minutes, without browning it. Whisk in flour and cook about 1 minute, stirring until smooth and lightly colored.
5. **Finish the sauce:** Use chicken broth, dried thyme, dried basil, heavy cream or half-and-half, and freshly grated Parmesan: gradually whisk broth into the roux with thyme and basil, loosening the browned fond. Simmer gently, whisking, until smooth and lightly thickened, about 1–2 minutes. Lower the heat and stir in cream and Parmesan, about 1–2 minutes, until the cheese melts. Do not boil hard after adding cheese. The sauce has contacted partly cooked chicken fond; wait until the final bake is complete before tasting it.
6. **Finish the chicken in sauce:** Stir the wilted spinach into the sauce and return the seared chicken skin-side up. Keep as much skin above the sauce as possible. If your oven-safe skillet cannot hold the thighs in one layer, transfer chicken, spinach and sauce to a baking dish large enough to fit them without overlap. Keep the roasted potatoes separate for crispness; adding them to the sauce will soften their surface.
7. **Bake and measure:** Transfer the skillet or chicken baking dish to the 425°F oven. Begin checking after about 10 minutes; the thickest part of every thigh, away from bone, and the sauce at the center must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue baking as needed; ten minutes is a first check, not a guarantee of completion. If the skin darkens early, shield it loosely with foil while the meat finishes. Check the separately roasted potatoes for tenderness as well. Rest safely cooked chicken 5 minutes before serving.
8. **Serve:** After the bake meets the temperature checks, taste the sauce with a clean spoon. Use salt, black pepper, and fresh parsley (if using): adjust salt and pepper, then add parsley if using. Serve one thigh per portion with potatoes, spinach and sauce.

## Potatoes Baked in the Sauce

For the baking-dish variation, omit the separate potato roast and its oil. Preheat to 400°F and lightly coat a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with the optional cooking spray. Sear the chicken and make the spinach and sauce as directed. Put chicken skin-side up in the dish, arrange the raw quartered potatoes and spinach around it and pour in the sauce. Bake about 25–30 minutes as a first check, then continue until every thigh and the sauce center reach 165°F / 74°C and potatoes are easily pierced. If safely cooked chicken finishes first, move it to a clean plate while the potatoes finish. Rest cooked chicken five minutes, then taste and season the safe sauce. Potatoes baked this way are soft and sauced. Add dishes as needed to keep the scaled chicken in one layer.

rootCorrections.before:
## Chef's Note

These chicken thighs finish in a garlic-Parmesan cream sauce with spinach, while the potatoes roast separately. Keep the potatoes beside the sauce at serving if you want their browned edges to remain crisp; sauce contact softens them. Brown the chicken first, then use temperature rather than skin color to judge the oven finish.

## Directions

1. **Start the potatoes:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. Set out cooking spray (if using), olive oil, and baby potatoes. Quarter the baby potatoes into similar pieces, toss with enough olive oil to coat, and spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet pan. Roast about 20–25 minutes, checking for browned edges and a center that yields easily to a knife; continue as needed. Check that all the measured thighs fit without overlap in your oven-safe skillet; use a baking dish for the chicken finish if needed. Prepare the chicken and sauce while the potatoes roast. The optional cooking spray is for the baking-dish variation below, which uses a different oven temperature and omits the separate potato roast.
2. **Brown the chicken:** Use bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, Italian seasoning, salt, black pepper, and unsalted butter: pat chicken dry with paper towels, then season with Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden, about 5–7 minutes, then brown the other side for about 2 minutes. Work in batches if needed, reducing heat if the butter or fond begins to burn. Transfer to a plate reserved for partly cooked chicken; continue directly with the recipe.
3. **Wilt the spinach:** Use unsalted butter and baby spinach: melt the butter for this step in the skillet, add spinach and stir until it begins to wilt, about 2 minutes. Transfer spinach to a bowl. Pour off excessive rendered chicken fat, keeping the browned fond and leaving no burned bits.
4. **Make the roux:** Use unsalted butter, garlic cloves, and all-purpose flour: melt the sauce butter over medium heat. Add garlic and stir until fragrant, about 1–2 minutes, without browning it. Whisk in flour and cook about 1 minute, stirring until smooth and lightly colored.
5. **Finish the sauce:** Use chicken broth, dried thyme, dried basil, heavy cream or half-and-half, and freshly grated Parmesan: gradually whisk broth into the roux with thyme and basil, loosening the browned fond. Simmer gently, whisking, until smooth and lightly thickened, about 1–2 minutes. Lower the heat and stir in cream and Parmesan, about 1–2 minutes, until the cheese melts. Do not boil hard after adding cheese. The sauce has contacted partly cooked chicken fond; wait until the final bake is complete before tasting it.
6. **Finish the chicken in sauce:** Stir the wilted spinach into the sauce and return the seared chicken skin-side up. Keep as much skin above the sauce as possible. If your oven-safe skillet cannot hold the thighs in one layer, transfer chicken, spinach and sauce to a baking dish large enough to fit them without overlap. Keep the roasted potatoes separate for crispness; adding them to the sauce will soften their surface.
7. **Bake and measure:** Transfer the skillet or chicken baking dish to the 425°F oven. Begin checking after about 10 minutes; the thickest part of every thigh, away from bone, and the sauce at the center must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue baking as needed; ten minutes is a first check, not a guarantee of completion. If the skin darkens early, shield it loosely with foil while the meat finishes. Check the separately roasted potatoes for tenderness as well. Rest safely cooked chicken 5 minutes before serving.
8. **Serve:** After the bake meets the temperature checks, taste the sauce with a clean spoon. Use salt, black pepper, and fresh parsley (if using): adjust salt and pepper, then add parsley if using. Serve one thigh per portion with potatoes, spinach and sauce.

## Potatoes Baked in the Sauce

For the baking-dish variation, omit the separate potato roast and its oil. Preheat to 400°F and lightly coat a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with the optional cooking spray. Sear the chicken and make the spinach and sauce as directed. Put chicken skin-side up in the dish, arrange the raw quartered potatoes and spinach around it and pour in the sauce. Bake about 25–30 minutes as a first check, then continue until every thigh and the sauce center reach 165°F / 74°C and potatoes are easily pierced. If safely cooked chicken finishes first, move it to a clean plate while the potatoes finish. Rest cooked chicken five minutes, then taste and season the safe sauce. Potatoes baked this way are soft and sauced. Add dishes as needed to keep the scaled chicken in one layer.
